applications.name: REA: Reverse Engineer Anything
applications.summary: Local CLI and MCP orchestration for source, binary and application investigation with evidence records and explicit unresolved questions.
applications.license: MIT (REA); external engines and analyzed artifacts retain separate terms
applications.pricing_notes: REA source is MIT; optional external commercial engines require their own licenses. No paid engine entitlement included.
applications.platform_notes: Provider and operation support differs by host. Read pinned provider prerequisites; this study did not run installers or engines.
features: CLI and MCP sharing binary-session composition
Provider-backed binary investigation and static application analysis
Digest-bound evidence and residual unknown history
Progressive tool discovery and lazy provider loading
strengths: Separates transport adapters from analysis providers
limitations: Selected source review only; no independent runtime or security certification
Depends on separately installed providers for many operations
Static evidence does not prove full behavior or recovered source equivalence
Per-platform and external engine restrictions apply

recommendation.pick_for: An authorized software investigation needs a consistent agent-facing interface and evidence trail across analysis providers.
recommendation.compare_when: Use underlying engines directly when their interactive workflow is more appropriate; benchmark REA with owned fixtures first.
